prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1439; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Insured reports both vehicles were traveling at low speed in opposite lanes when contact occurred. Police report requested. Claimant is represented by counsel; letter of representation received and logged. All further contact to be routed through counsel.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office regarding the injury claim. Counsel reports claimant is experiencing lower back strain and has sought outpatient care. Requested medical records and provider information, along with a signed authorization form. Counsel indicated records will follow.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos of both vehicles submitted by the insured. Front bumper damage consistent with low-speed impact. No airbag deployment reported on either vehicle. Sent vehicle to independent appraiser for estimate. Noted that the other driver's carrier has been placed on notice.

Entry 4: Received medical documentation from claimant's provider through counsel. Diagnosis is lumbar strain with recommended physical therapy. Treatment is ongoing and prognosis is listed as favorable. Forwarded records to medical review for evaluation of causation and reasonableness of treatment. Will request an independent review if treatment duration extends.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant's counsel to confirm receipt of appraisal and status of treatment. Counsel advised claimant continues physical therapy and reports reduced pain. Requested updated treatment notes and any wage loss documentation. File remains open pending medical review and liability determination.
